# Language navigation

**Status:** Trial  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Language navigation to let users identify the current language and switch to equivalent versions offered by the service.

## When to use

- Use when the service offers equivalent content or journeys in more than one language.
- Keep the switcher consistently placed and preserve journey state where the service can do so safely.

## When not to use

- Do not show a language as available when the linked page or journey is incomplete.
- Do not use country flags to represent languages.

## Anatomy

- **Language navigation landmark (required):** A nav has a localised aria-label describing the language choice.
- **Language list (required):** A list contains one item for each offered language.
- **Current language (required):** Non-link text has aria-current=true and an accurate lang attribute.
- **Alternative links (required):** Each link uses rel=alternate, lang and hreflang for the target language.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `nav` | `govuk-language-navigation` | A small language set on a standard background. |
| Inverse | `nav` | `govuk-language-navigation`, `govuk-language-navigation--inverse` | A supported dark-background location with verified contrast. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The component requires no GOV.UK JavaScript and all alternative links must be ordinary href navigation.
- Retain relevant user data across language changes only where privacy, validation and service design allow it.
- Review this Trial component when updating GOV.UK Frontend because its guidance or API may change.

## Accessibility contract

- Write each language name in that language and set lang so assistive technology pronounces it correctly.
- Set dir on items when scripts have different writing directions.
- Localise the navigation label and any visually hidden language-description text.

## Content rules

- Use the native name for each language, for example “Cymraeg”.
- Do not abbreviate language names unless research shows the abbreviation is understood.
- Keep equivalent pages aligned so switching language does not unexpectedly change the task.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`

## HTML examples

### English and Welsh navigation

```html
<nav class="govuk-language-navigation" aria-label="Language">
  <ul class="govuk-language-navigation__list">
    <li class="govuk-language-navigation__list-item"><span class="govuk-language-navigation__text" aria-current="true" lang="en">English</span></li>
    <li class="govuk-language-navigation__list-item"><a class="govuk-language-navigation__link" href="/cy" rel="alternate" lang="cy" hreflang="cy">Cymraeg</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```
